summary: Add customer_note column, backfill, deploy new, retire old, drop note, with a sync trigger to maintain cross-version consistency during concurrent traffic.
write_consistency: An AFTER UPDATE trigger on account_user synchronizes note and customer_note: when either column changes, the other is updated to match, ensuring reads from either version always see the latest write.
revision_notes: The previous plan failed during deploy_new because a single backfill could not maintain consistency when old and new versions concurrently wrote to separate columns (note vs customer_note), causing the runner's interleaved read/write assertions to read stale seed data. Root cause: absence of an ongoing synchronization mechanism between the two columns during concurrent traffic.

stages.description: Add customer_note column and a trigger to sync note and customer_note.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user ADD COLUMN customer_note TEXT NULL;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note() RETURNS $$ BEGIN IF NEW.note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.note THEN NEW.customer_note := NEW.note; ELSIF NEW.customer_note IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.customer_note THEN NEW.note := NEW.customer_note; END IF; RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER sync_note_customer_note AFTER UPDATE ON account_user FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION sync_note_customer_note();

stages.description: Copy existing note values into customer_note so new code sees data.
Deploy the new application version (new-staged) which now references customer_note instead of note.
Retire the old application version (old). After this stage, only the new version serves traffic.
Remove the old note column after the old app is retired and customer_note is populated.
sql: ALTER TABLE account_user DROP COLUMN note;
